n: Be generous and take wise risks, even when the return seems uncertain. Like grain shipped across the sea, kindness and investment often come back in time.

f.w: Cast thy bread upon the waters
f.g: Possibly sea trade or generous giving; both readings teach bold, faithful generosity.

n: Share with many people — seven, even eight — because you don’t know what hardships may come. Generosity builds a safety net of goodwill.

f.g: A Hebrew way of saying “many, and then some more.”

n: Some things just happen according to nature: full clouds pour rain, and a fallen tree stays where it lands. We can’t control everything.
If you wait for perfect weather, you’ll never plant or harvest. Too much caution leads to doing nothing.
Just as we don’t understand how life forms in the womb, we can’t understand all of God’s works. Trust Him and act anyway.

f.g: Hebrew ruach — wind, breath, or spirit; how life enters a baby.

f.w: bones do grow in the womb

n: Work diligently morning and evening, since you never know which effort will succeed — or whether both will.
Life is sweet; it is a joy to see the light of the sun. The Preacher affirms the goodness of being alive.
However long you live, enjoy every year, but remember that dark days will also come. Everything ahead is fleeting.

f.g: Old age, hardship, and finally death.

n: Young people should enjoy their youth and follow their heart’s good desires — while remembering that God will hold them accountable for their choices.

f.w: God will bring thee into judgment

n: So put away worry and avoid what harms your body, because youth passes quickly.

f.g: Youth is a fleeting breath — use it well.

f.w: put away evil from thy flesh
